sub_type: multi-user developer framework/toolkit for agent harness engineering

categories.aliases: error handling / exception handling / error messages / graceful failure
categories.day1_tell: Feed it malformed input and a dead dependency; confirm a useful error, not a stack trace or silent wrong answer.
categories.reasoning: Adapter and MCP/store error types exist, but evidence shows at least one example store still leaks a bare KeyError and there is not enough evidence that all malformed/dead-dependency paths return user-oriented errors.

fix_sites.what: Replace the bare KeyError path with a domain NotFound error and add a regression test for the public error surface.
Add tests for malformed adapter output and dead subprocess/dependency failures asserting clean AdapterError messages without tracebacks.

categories.aliases: logging / log levels / debug output / diagnostics
categories.day1_tell: Reproduce a failure and confirm the logs alone are enough to localize it (level, context, no secrets).
categories.reasoning: The repo emphasizes redacted receipts and diagnostics in docs/tests, but the evidence does not show a consistent logging policy or structured failure logs sufficient to localize failures across the runtime.

fix_sites.what: Document diagnostic log fields, levels, redaction rules, and how to reproduce/localize MCP failures from logs.
Assert failed CLI commands emit structured context and no secrets while avoiding raw stack traces for expected failures.

categories.aliases: input validation / sanitization / malformed input handling
categories.day1_tell: Send hostile input (oversized, wrong type, injection-shaped) at every external boundary and confirm rejection.
categories.reasoning: External boundaries such as adapters, CLI/project policy, orchestrator, and runtime are represented in code and tests, with evidence of explicit parsing and validation of input fields and usage values.

categories.aliases: configuration / config files / settings / environment variables / defaults
categories.day1_tell: Boot with zero config (sane defaults), then override one value via file AND env var; confirm precedence is documented.
categories.reasoning: Configuration is treated as a first-class concern with defaults, ignored local config, environment-variable/private config guidance, and portable profile separation documented and implemented in config.py.

categories.aliases: documentation / README / usage docs / examples
categories.day1_tell: A new user completes install → first successful use from the README alone, no source reading.
categories.reasoning: README and CLI/setup docs provide installation and first-use paths, and contributing/ops docs reinforce deterministic checks for a new user workflow.

categories.aliases: tests / unit tests / integration tests / test fixes
categories.day1_tell: Run the test suite from a fresh clone with one documented command; confirm it exercises the core path, not just helpers.
categories.reasoning: The repo has substantial tests across core project, ops, swarm, traces, and documented CI/test expectations, indicating core paths are exercised rather than only helpers.

categories.aliases: continuous integration / build pipeline / release automation
categories.day1_tell: Push a failing commit and confirm CI blocks it; push a tag and confirm an artifact is produced.
categories.reasoning: Woodpecker CI is referenced and release/packaging automation exists, but the supplied evidence does not directly show push/tag workflows blocking failing commits and producing artifacts.

fix_sites.what: Add an explicit CI/CD section describing required Woodpecker pipelines for pushes and tags and the artifact produced by each.
Link to the CI status and release artifact workflow so users can verify failing commits are blocked and tags build packages.

categories.aliases: dependency updates / version bumps / library upgrades / dependabot / renovate / automated updates
categories.day1_tell: Confirm dependencies are pinned/lockfiled and an automated update mechanism (or documented cadence) exists.
categories.reasoning: Dependency awareness appears in roadmap and code, but the evidence does not establish pinned/locked dependencies or an automated update mechanism/documented cadence.

fix_sites.what: Document the dependency pinning/lockfile policy and the cadence or tool used for dependency updates.
Add a short operator note explaining how dependency versions are verified for installed releases.

categories.aliases: performance / speed / memory usage / optimization
categories.day1_tell: Run the core operation on a realistic-sized input and confirm latency/memory are measured, not assumed.
categories.reasoning: Performance and cost are acknowledged in roadmap/usage code, but evidence does not show measured latency or memory benchmarks on realistic-sized workflows.

fix_sites.what: Add current benchmark targets/results for realistic workflow sizes, including latency, memory, and cost envelopes.
Extend usage metrics to record runtime duration and bounded resource measurements where available.

categories.aliases: security / vulnerability fix / secrets handling / permissions
categories.day1_tell: Grep for secrets in repo/logs (none), confirm least-privilege defaults, and run a dependency audit clean.
categories.reasoning: Security policy and least-privilege design are visible, but the evidence does not prove secret scanning and dependency audit are clean or enforced.

fix_sites.what: Record the required secret-scan and dependency-audit gates and their current pass/fail expectations.
Add a maintainer checklist for secret exposure checks and dependency vulnerability audit before release.

categories.aliases: packaging / install / distribution / setup
categories.day1_tell: Install via the documented package-manager path on a clean machine and run the entry point.
categories.reasoning: Packaging and clean installation are explicitly tested and release-gated, including wheel/sdist build, isolated install, entry point execution, and Woodpecker packaging CI.

categories.aliases: versioning / semver / version tagging / release cadence
categories.day1_tell: Confirm released versions are tagged, semver-meaningful, and the running binary reports its version.
categories.reasoning: The changelog declares Semantic Versioning, release tags are referenced, and tests/docs cover running package and contract version reporting.

categories.aliases: retries / timeouts / backoff / transient failure handling
categories.day1_tell: Kill a dependency mid-call: confirm bounded timeout, backoff retry, and a clean failure after exhaustion.
categories.reasoning: CLI and runtime evidence includes explicit timeout flags, bounded retry/repair semantics, and tests for runtime and routing behavior under failure.

categories.aliases: cache / caching layer / cache invalidation
categories.day1_tell: Identify what is cached, force staleness, and confirm invalidation works (no permanently wrong answers).
categories.reasoning: Loop and CLI tests imply stateful/retry behavior, but the evidence does not clearly identify cache contents, staleness forcing, or invalidation guarantees.

fix_sites.what: Document and expose the exact cached evidence/state keys and the invalidation conditions.
Add a stale-evidence test proving changed inputs invalidate cached loop decisions.
Clarify whether caching is in scope for the runtime and what correctness invariant prevents stale answers.

categories.aliases: metrics / monitoring / observability / usage tracking
categories.day1_tell: Confirm the system emits enough signal (metrics/health/structured logs) to detect it being broken without a user report.
categories.reasoning: For a local developer framework, telemetry is implemented as local usage/metrics and CLI stats rather than phone-home monitoring, with tests and documentation for usage telemetry and derived graph metrics.

categories.aliases: auth / login / API keys / access control
categories.day1_tell: Attempt the privileged operation unauthenticated and as a wrong-role user; both must fail safely.
categories.reasoning: This is a local/keyless developer CLI and framework; sub-type-appropriate authority is profile/tool scope rather than end-user authentication or role login flows.

categories.aliases: database / persistence / schema migration / data integrity
categories.day1_tell: Upgrade from a previous-version data dir/schema and confirm data survives; kill -9 mid-write and confirm no corruption.
categories.reasoning: Persistence, lifecycle state, and artifacts are central, but evidence does not show migration tests from previous schema versions or kill-9/atomic-write corruption tests.

fix_sites.what: Add explicit schema versioning and migration hooks for durable run state.
Add crash/partial-write regression coverage proving artifact receipts remain valid or fail closed.
Document the data migration and crash-consistency guarantees for run state.

categories.aliases: user interface / usability / display fixes / formatting
categories.day1_tell: Walk the golden path as a first-time user; confirm empty states, long values, and errors all render intentionally.
categories.reasoning: For a CLI/toolkit, UX polish maps to command behavior, help/error surfaces, safety messages, and contributor-visible workflow docs, all represented in CLI tests and docs.

categories.aliases: i18n / localization / translations
categories.day1_tell: Feed non-ASCII input end-to-end (CJK, emoji, RTL) and confirm no mangling; locale strings externalized if user-facing.
categories.reasoning: No evidence mentions internationalization, localization, translations, or Unicode/non-ASCII handling, so the sub-type-relevant Unicode data path is unproven.

fix_sites.what: Add an end-to-end CLI test using CJK, emoji, and RTL text in workflow/project inputs and assert JSON/output round-trips without mangling.
Document UTF-8 input/output expectations and terminal/JSON encoding behavior.

categories.aliases: resource leaks / file handles / memory cleanup / shutdown handling
categories.day1_tell: Run a soak loop and confirm stable handles/memory; SIGTERM mid-work and confirm graceful shutdown.
categories.reasoning: The design uses scoped worktrees, SQLite state, and bounded execution, but the evidence does not show soak-loop resource stability or SIGTERM cleanup behavior.

fix_sites.what: Add SIGTERM/SIGINT handling that closes stores, terminates child processes, and records an interrupted lifecycle event.
Add cleanup tests for interrupted runs ensuring temp worktrees/files and subprocesses are not leaked.
Add a resource-cleanup acceptance criterion covering soak runs and signal interruption.

categories.aliases: SECURITY.md / vulnerability reporting / disclosure policy / security contact
categories.day1_tell: Find the documented vulnerability-reporting channel (SECURITY.md) and confirm a reporter could use it without filing a public issue.
categories.reasoning: SECURITY.md clearly tells reporters not to open public issues and to use GitHub private vulnerability reporting or the configured security contact.

categories.aliases: LICENSE / license metadata / copyright / third-party notices
categories.day1_tell: Confirm a LICENSE file exists and the package metadata declares the same license.
categories.reasoning: Release gate requires license files, packaging tests inspect metadata, and NOTICE/roadmap document MIT licensing and provenance obligations.

categories.aliases: CONTRIBUTING / code of conduct / issue templates / PR templates
categories.day1_tell: From CONTRIBUTING.md alone, a new contributor can set up, run tests, and submit a change.
categories.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md provides setup/change expectations and links release rules, while README/pyproject/CI evidence supports contributor test and submission workflow.

categories.aliases: CHANGELOG / keep-a-changelog / dated release notes / breaking-change notes
categories.day1_tell: Open the changelog: latest release has a dated, sectioned entry that calls out breaking changes separately.
categories.reasoning: A changelog exists with SemVer and release links, but the evidence only shows an alpha release entry area and does not prove dated sectioned notes with breaking changes called out separately for the latest release.

fix_sites.what: Ensure each release has a dated section with standard subsections and an explicit Breaking Changes subsection, even when empty.
Add a release-gate checklist item requiring dated changelog entries and separate breaking-change notes.

categories.aliases: lint / linter / static analysis / formatter / type checking in CI
categories.day1_tell: Run the project's lint/typecheck command locally and confirm CI enforces the same check.
categories.reasoning: Static validation, lint/type expectations, verify-mcp checks, and CI/release enforcement are documented and represented in source/tests.

categories.aliases: signed releases / checksums / sigstore / SLSA / build provenance
categories.day1_tell: Download a release artifact and verify its checksum or signature by the documented method.
categories.reasoning: Release artifacts are linked and provenance is discussed, but documented checksum/signature verification for downloaded artifacts is not shown in the evidence.

fix_sites.what: Document the checksum or signature generation and verification commands for release artifacts.
Add a short verification step next to the wheel download command using the published checksum/signature.

categories.aliases: SBOM / software bill of materials / dependency disclosure
categories.day1_tell: Generate or locate the published SBOM for the latest release.
categories.reasoning: SBOM generation is listed as a roadmap/release goal, but there is no evidence of an existing generated or published SBOM for the latest release.

fix_sites.what: Mark SBOM generation as an implemented release gate only when a concrete SBOM artifact path and tool are added.
Add the SBOM generation command and publication location for each release.

categories.aliases: fuzz testing / property-based tests / fuzzers
categories.day1_tell: Find a fuzz or property-based target exercising the main parser/input boundary; run it briefly.
categories.reasoning: The evidence shows tests and validation docs but no fuzzing or property-based target for the main workflow/parser/input boundaries.

fix_sites.what: Add fuzz/property-based parser testing as a concrete quality gate with target inputs and runtime budget.
Document any trace/workflow corpus or generator used for randomized parser and analyzer testing.

categories.aliases: upgrade guide / UPGRADING.md / deprecation warnings / breaking-change policy
categories.day1_tell: Trigger a deprecated path: it warns with the removal version and a migration pointer; an upgrade guide exists.
categories.reasoning: Migration and protocol-breaking changes are discussed, but evidence does not show a formal deprecation policy with warnings, removal versions, and migration pointers in code paths.

fix_sites.what: Add a deprecation policy requiring warning text, removal version, and migration link for any deprecated CLI/schema path.
Introduce a standard deprecation warning helper for old project/schema fields with removal-version metadata.
Link to an upgrade/deprecation section for users crossing breaking protocol or schema changes.

categories.aliases: privacy policy / data collection disclosure / telemetry opt-out
categories.day1_tell: Find documentation of what data is collected/stored and a working opt-out for any telemetry.
categories.reasoning: Local usage telemetry is present and release-gated, but the evidence does not show a privacy/data-handling disclosure or opt-out behavior for collected local telemetry.

fix_sites.what: Document exactly what usage data is stored locally, where it is stored, retention expectations, and how to disable or delete it.
Add or document a no-usage-telemetry option/env var and ensure stats commands report the current telemetry setting.
Expose the telemetry opt-out capability/state in the capability manifest.
